items.title: At $729 billion, forex kitty hits a record
items.summary: Reserves increased $12.4 billion during the week, with foreign currency assets increasing $9.4 billion to $591 billion, while the value of gold reserves rose by $2.8 billion to $114 billion. Forex reserves last touched a high of $728 billion late February this year. As of August 21, Indian banks have mobilised $65.4 billion in foreign currency non-resident (FCNR-B) deposits under the Reserve Bank of India's special forex swap facility. Total foreign exchange inflows through this specific window reached $72.85 billion, the RBI said in a statement.

items.title: TVS Motor names global biz head Peyman Kargar as next chief executive
items.summary: Kargar will take over as director and CEO from K N Radhakrishnan on January 27, 2027, TVS Motor said on Friday. Radhakrishnan will continue as CEO until then and subsequently serve as a non-executive director till the company's annual general meeting scheduled for July 2027. The leadership change comes after TVS Motor sold 5.9 million vehicles globally in FY26 and reported 30% revenue growth.

items.summary: Coal India has raised concerns about the coal gasification incentive scheme's rules. The company believes the short bidding window disadvantages state-run firms. Excluding captive power plants from eligible costs also creates a disadvantage. Coal India requested a six-month application period for the initial round. The ministry rejected this, citing immediate subsequent bidding rounds.

items.summary: Apple raised prices for Apple Music by $1 per month in July, citing licensing costs.

items.title: Food safety eateries' body says fix the problem, not the blame
items.summary: Several prominent Indian restaurants face hygiene violation allegations from consumers and regulators. NRAI president emphasizes fixing problems and fair enforcement over blame and reputational damage. Social media scrutiny and regulatory actions are impacting well-known food establishments across the country. Enforcement must follow legal procedures, offering businesses a chance to rectify issues. This situation highlights the ongoing need for stringent food safety standards and transparent oversight.

items.title: Peg by peg, Vodka's share is rising in India
items.summary: Vodka is capturing a record share of India's liquor market, driven by younger consumers and women. This trend marks a significant structural shift towards white spirits, especially vodka. Radico Khaitan's vodka business has seen substantial growth over the past five years. The company has also focused on premiumizing its whisky portfolio to adapt. This strategic move reduces dependence on lower-priced liquor and commodity selling.

items.title: CNG price hiked by Rs 3.89/kg in Delhi-NCR amid West Asia crisis
items.summary: New CNG price: Indraprastha Gas Limited has raised compressed natural gas prices by Rs 3.89 per kilogram. This price adjustment took effect on Saturday, impacting Delhi-NCR consumers significantly. The increase reflects higher import costs for liquefied natural gas amid global energy price fluctuations. Consequently, freight and passenger fares across the region are expected to see an upward revision. This marks the fifth CNG price hike in Delhi-NCR this year.

items.title: Maharashtra sugarcane farmers seek higher prices after sugar rally
items.summary: Sugarcane farmers in Maharashtra are demanding higher prices for the 2025-26 season. This agitation follows a significant increase in sugar prices over recent months. Farmer organizations believe sugar mills should share increased profits with growers. Several farmer associations have submitted their demands to the state sugar commissionerate. Growers across the state seek better payment for sugarcane sold to mills.

items.title: Treasury moves to sanction UAE branch of Egyptian bank over Iran ties
items.summary: Banque Misr UAE processed about $1.8 billion over two years for some 100 companies that are potentially part of Iran's shadow banking network, Treasury said.

items.title: OIL, IOCL exit Gabon block, end decade-old oil project
items.summary: Oil India and Indian Oil have relinquished their Shakthi-II exploration block in Gabon. This action terminates their Production Sharing Contract with the country's Directorate General of Hydrocarbons. The project began with an oil discovery over a decade ago. However, repeated delays ultimately led to the block's relinquishment. Both companies had entered the block in an equal fifty-fifty partnership.

items.title: India, Canada ready to fast-track bilateral investment treaty talks
items.summary: India and Canada will start bilateral investment treaty negotiations soon. Both nations will explore cross-border payment system collaborations and critical mineral partnerships. They aim to broaden the use of UPI in Canada through payment provider alliances. This dialogue builds on prior commitments to strengthen economic and financial cooperation. The countries aspire to increase bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion by 2030.

items.title: Sugar supply likely to improve on switch to fortnightly quota
items.summary: Under the fortnightly quota, sugar mills will be required to sell at least 40% of the allocation in the first week and the remaining quantity in the succeeding week. It was observed that in certain cases, sugar sold by mills at the beginning of the month was being dispatched or lifted by buyers only towards the end of the month, leading to artificial scarcity, the government said in a statement.

items.title: Renewable energy projects can now store and sell curtailed power using co-located battery systems
items.summary: The renewable energy landscape is evolving as the power ministry allows the storage of curtailed electricity from renewable projects. This stored energy can be harnessed to charge on-site battery systems, enabling developers to independently sell this surplus power via power exchanges. This initiative not only enhances the effective use of renewable energy generation but also opens doors for monetizing energy that would otherwise go to waste.

items.title: Industrial output grows 6.7% in July
items.summary: India's industrial output saw a 6.7% growth in July. Manufacturing output increased by 7.3% year-on-year during the same period. Electricity generation also rose by 8.7% in July. Consumer durables surged to an eight-month high, driving overall growth. Capital goods output also showed a significant increase.

The appointment comes as Old Navy struggles with falling comparable sales, while Gap's other brands gain momentum. Investors are betting on a turnaround at the company's biggest brand.

items.summary: India's market regulator is considering new rules for small business public offerings. These potential changes include quotas for institutional investors ahead of share sales. The regulator may also raise listing size limits and profit requirements for these firms. These proposed adjustments follow concerns about fund diversion and high fees. Such moves aim to enhance governance and investor protection in the segment.
